attrs.reason: Management claims 51% DTC revenue growth drove receivables decline and CFO increase, but the evidence pack contains no segment revenue data to verify the DTC growth rate or its magnitude relative to the receivables/CFO changes. The pattern (lower DSO, higher CFO) is consistent with a shift to cash-based sales, but the named driver (DTC growth) is not visible in the reported numbers; it rests on management's word (E38).

rebuttal.innocent_explanation: The 51% DTC revenue growth reported by management (E38) shifts a larger portion of sales to cash-based direct-to-consumer channels, which inherently reduces accounts receivable and days sales outstanding while increasing operating cash flow relative to net income. The financial signals confirm this pattern: revenue grew 10.1% (E13 vs E1) while receivables fell 2.2% (E19 vs E7), DSO improved from 45 to 40 days (E25), quarterly DSO declined each quarter (E27-E30), and operating cash flow jumped 55.8% (E18 vs E6) versus net income growth of 21.5% (E17 vs E5).
